title: Prompt Problems in Promptly
summary: CS1 and CS2 students infer programming requirements from visual examples and write a natural-language prompt that makes an LLM generate correct Python code. Generated code is automatically tested, and students iteratively revise only the prompt until all tests pass.

sources.title: Prompt Problems: A New Programming Exercise for the Generative AI Era
sources.evidence_quote: A student solves a Prompt Problem by crafting a natural language prompt which, when provided as input to an LLM, outputs code that successfully solves a specified programming task.

assessment.summary: Interpret a visual input/output specification and construct a prompt that causes ChatGPT to generate a passing Python program or function.
student_actions: Infer the general computational task from visual examples.
Inspect generated code and test feedback.
Revise the prompt until the generated code passes.

outputs.artifact: LLM-generated code passing the instructor tests

student_role.description: The task is completed by writing prompts for the integrated LLM; students cannot edit the generated code.

allowed_purposes: code generation from a student-authored prompt

grading.method: Ungraded optional lab; the system reports success when generated code passes the full test suite.
process: Only the first failing test is shown after an unsuccessful attempt.
Students must solve each problem to progress to the next.

reported_results: 58 of 414 CS1 students and 182 of 444 CS2 students attempted at least one problem.
Success rates for individual problems ranged from 65% to 99% among students attempting them.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
